title.narrative: Strengthening national capacity for implementing the enhanced transparency framework in Samoa

description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

The Samoa Capacity Building Initiative for Transparency (CBIT) project is designed to deliver significant socio-economic benefits by enhancing the nation’s capacity to manage and report on climate actions effectively. One of the primary benefits is the creation of new job opportunities and career development for individuals involved in transparency-related roles. By institutionalizing roles and responsibilities within the GHG inventory and MRV frameworks, the project fosters career growth and skill development for government officials, industry professionals, and community members.Enhanced climate resilience is another key benefit, protecting livelihoods and reducing economic losses from extreme weather events like cyclones. By improving data collection and reporting systems, the project ensures Samoa's adaptation and mitigation strategies are based on accurate information, leading to more effective climate policies, actions and decision making. This increased resilience supports food security, water management, and infrastructure protection, which are vital for the well-being and economic stability of local communities.Additionally, the project stimulates economic growth by promoting investments in green technologies and renewable energy. By enhancing the GHG inventory and MRV frameworks, the CBIT project creates opportunities for developing renewable energy projects and improving energy efficiency. These initiatives not only reduce greenhouse gas emissions but also create jobs and foster new skills within the local workforce. The focus on capacity building ensures that government officials, industry leaders, and community members are well-equipped to engage in and benefit from these green initiatives, thus driving sustainable economic development.Moreover, the CBIT project enhances governance and institutional capacity, leading to more effective public administration and greater public trust. By clearly defining roles and improving coordination among various stakeholders, the project ensures that climate actions are integrated into national planning and budget processes. This improved governance framework supports international cooperation and attracts additional funding and technical assistance, increasing the project's socio-economic impact. Overall, the Samoa CBIT project not only addresses climate change challenges but also contributes to a more resilient, sustainable, and economically vibrant future for the nation.
To strengthen institutional, technical and human capacities to enable Samoa to comply with the requirements of the transparency framework under the Paris Agreement.
